title: Mask: live filters, a real run and verified overlay export
description: Use the real downloadable microscopy example, test live area and diameter changes, run two fields with Plot enabled, and recover a missing overlay through an explicit Python plotting workaround.
objectives: Find Mask on Home and its nested Live, Time and 3D controls.
Check source metadata and channel identities before testing segmentation.
Distinguish a reversible display filter from a model-parameter rerun.
Inspect genuine batch output, preserve the partial-overlay warning and export both arrays explicitly.
Keep QC limitations, original data and an unsent AI question distinct from scientific validation.
prerequisite: Use the actual Mask download, retaining known channel identities and filename metadata. Preserved live-preview footage is reused only after confirming live_preview.py and preview_contract.py are byte-identical to their recorded source; its saved masks independently reproduce 51→25→51 at minimum area 5642 and 42 after diameter 30→60. The new two-field batch is a separate example, not a direct count benchmark: Plot=True, test_images=2, batch_size=2, n_jobs=2, diameters 30/30/15 and explicit cell/nucleus/pathogen flow thresholds 0.4. Archive value 100 disables flow filtering and is not taught as recommended. The native overlay loop STILL fails on .spacr_plane_layout.json: one of two overlays is missing despite Finished. Do not delete the layout or enable pickle loading. The linked helper calls spacr.plot.plot_image_mask_overlay on regular .npy files only, requiring four intensity planes followed by cell/nucleus/pathogen at 4/5/6. It writes a new opaque-background PNG folder, never changes source arrays, and does not fix the GUI loop. Both source array hashes match the native run journal. Final labels are 25/19/8 and 52/50/58; first-field pathogen QC warns near_empty_field. Cell QC precedes mask adjustment. Independent checks cover 95,424,864 channel RGB array values and 7,952,072 combined-foreground pixels, not biological accuracy. Previous failed runs and transparent-plot probes are preserved but not presented as complete. No AI request, training, scientific approval or publication. API: spacr.core.preprocess_generate_masks and spacr.plot.plot_image_mask_overlay. OPS remains unproven and is not taught here.

scenes.narration: Open Mask from Home. It is a main module; Live, Time and three-dimensional settings are reached inside it. Time has its own linked tutorial under Mask in the submodule section. This lesson covers a two-dimensional example, live comparisons and a plotting workaround, not an automatically validated segmentation.

Click Load test data and let the real microscopy example finish downloading. Keep its folder structure and original images. The recording uses a fresh private copy, so a previous run cannot supply stale results. For your own data, confirm the filename metadata and channel identities before copying any example settings.

Here nucleus intensity is channel zero, cell intensity is channel one, and pathogen intensity is channel two. The example also contains channel three. These are intensity-channel identities, not the mask-plane numbers in a merged output. Check the images themselves and retain the layout metadata when moving results.

Turn on Live and select a field for inspection. Preview is where you compare the image with the proposed masks before a larger run. The preserved preview uses a different field from the two batch fields shown later. A displayed preview count is not directly comparable with a batch total.

Open Live settings and inspect the cell controls. This recording uses the installed CPSAM model; available model choices depend on your installation. Run the preview before interpreting its outlines. Diameter and filtering controls are different operations, and neither the selected model name nor a colourful mask guarantees accuracy.

The baseline contains fifty-one cell labels. Raising minimum area to five thousand six hundred forty-two pixels leaves twenty-five visible labels. This is a reversible filter of the existing result: the raw mask stays unchanged and the model is not rerun. The threshold is a demonstration, not an optimal biological cutoff.

Restore the original area limit and all fifty-one labels return. Inspect which objects disappear and why before adopting a filter. Small objects may be genuine objects or segmentation errors; removing them does not itself answer that question. Keep the raw result and the chosen filter values separately identifiable.

Changing diameter from thirty to sixty pixels and running again is a model-parameter comparison, not just a display filter. This produces forty-two labels in the recorded field. Compare boundaries with the image, not only the count. Fewer labels do not establish a better model, and these settings are not a universal recommendation.

For the separate batch, use two test images and keep Plot enabled. Here all three flow thresholds are explicitly zero point four. The downloaded settings had one hundred, which disables flow filtering; we do not recommend that value by default. Review the console's device and processing messages instead of assuming how the run executed.

Read the whole console. Although the worker says Finished, the overlay ledger reports one of two plots missing: it tried to load the layout JSON as an image. The merged mask arrays exist, but this is not a complete native plotting run. Keep the warning and do not silently treat it as success.

The workaround is an explicit external step. Keep the layout JSON: it describes the intensity and mask planes and is not an image. Never enable pickle loading to silence this error. Download the linked helper, inspect it, and use the merged folder belonging to this particular run, not an older result directory.

Run the helper with the merged source and a new destination. It calls the real plotting API separately for each numeric array and saves both overlays. It refuses a different plane layout or an existing output folder. This bypasses the faulty directory scan for this export; it does not repair the application's plotting loop.

These are the saved plots in an external image viewer, not figures inserted into spaCR. The first field has twenty-five cell, nineteen nucleus and eight pathogen labels after adjustment. Its pathogen QC still warns that eight objects are too few for the per-field size checks. A readable overlay does not remove that limitation.

The second field has fifty-two cell, fifty nucleus and fifty-eight pathogen labels. The first four panels show the recorded intensity channels and their outlines; the last combines the object masks. Percentile normalization here is for display only. The source arrays are unchanged, and these label counts are not ground-truth accuracy measurements.

Keep the output checks, original journal, settings and QC files together. We independently checked the plotted channel arrays, combined foreground coverage and unchanged source hashes. Cell QC was recorded before cell-mask adjustment, so its counts need not equal the final merged counts. Inspect segmentation quality yourself before continuing to Measure.

The console's optional spaCR AI control can help you discuss settings, but this example question is unsent and no provider answer is shown. Verify any advice against the real files and warnings. The Python pipeline and per-file plotting API follow the same data contracts; the linked lessons cover measurement and the nested time workflow.
